newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche's Breuer - EMU will lead to fewer bourses.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's Breuer - EMU will lead to fewer bourses.

text.p: The advent of European monetary union will lead to the closure of some of Europe's bourses, Rolf Breuer, supervisory board chairman at the German stock exchange company Deutsche Boerse AG, said on Friday.

"Only the best will survive," Breuer told a conference examining the future of Europe's bourses post-EMU, adding that monetary union will lead to the development of one of the world's largest supranational financial markets.
There are currently 32 official stock exchanges in Europe, but Breuer said that will not be the case post EMU.
"I see more centralisation and a trend towards integration and cooperation taking place," said Breuer, who also sits on the Deutsche Bank management board.
European currency union will accelerate the pace of change in Europe's various financial centres and an integrated capital market requires fewer bourses than currently, Breuer said.
Share markets had a good chance of survival if they worked efficiently, attached worth to a good infrastructure and made dealing as user-friendly as possible.
If this didn't happen, dealers would choose other financial centres or examine other possible trading alternatives.

In terms of debt markets, the main issue was not so much where the largest volumes will be traded, but who can offer the best market for underlying instruments on the Euro contract. This applied in particular to repurchase agreements.
"The future belongs to whoever has the most effective repo market," Breuer said.
